name: Cost Management Plan
purpose: A part of the project management plan that says how project costs will be estimated, structured, monitored and controlled. It fixes the measuring conventions (units, rounding, accuracy), the thresholds and rules used later for cost control, and the reporting format. The prose adds that it may also carry authority levels for cost and budget commitment, funding limitations, and guidance on when and how costs are recorded. It is developed once and does not usually change.

elements.guidance: How each type of resource is measured: labor in staff hours, days or weeks; physical resources in gallons, meters, tons or whatever suits the material; some resources are a lump sum each time they are used.
Whether estimates are rounded to hundreds, thousands or another step.
The accuracy the estimates need. It may change as more is known (progressive elaboration); where rolling wave planning guidelines exist, give the accuracy required at each stage as time passes.
Cost estimating and reporting follow the WBS numbering and, where required, the organization's code of accounts or other accounting and reporting structures.

The measures that decide whether an activity, work package or the whole project is on budget, needs preventive action, or is over budget and needs corrective action; usually a percent deviation from the baseline.

The WBS level at which progress and spending are measured; for earned value, whether costs are reported at work package or control account level; the measurement method (weighted milestones, fixed formula, percent complete and so on); and the equations that will forecast estimate to complete (ETC) and estimate at completion (EAC).
The cost information needed for status and progress reports, a copy of or reference to any required format or template, and the reporting frequency.
Variables behind strategic funding choices such as make or buy, buy or lease, borrowing versus in-house funds.

tailoring: On smaller projects the project manager often does not manage the budget; in that case the form is not needed.
Units of measure for each type of resource may sit in this plan or in the resource management plan (2.26).

On projects that use earned value management, add the rules for setting percent complete and the EVM measurement techniques (fixed formula, percent complete, level of effort and so on); on projects that do not, delete that field.

citation: Book of Forms form 2.19, PDF pages 93 to 94 (printed pages 82 to 83)
notes: The prose lists eight things the plan can include; three of them (process for estimating costs, process for developing a time-phased budget, process for monitoring and controlling costs) have no box on the blank form (PDF page 95, printed page 84), and neither do the optional extras (authority levels, funding limitations, cost recording guidelines). The prose table says 'Cost reporting information and format'; the blank form prints 'Cost Reporting and Format', which wins. The alignment list (charter, schedule management plan) is shorter than the receives list, which also names the risk management plan. The prose gives no section on adaptive projects.
